message.content:
### Tenant Rights in Texas (as of 2026) | Area | What You’re Entitled To | Key Points | |------|------------------------|------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Must be returned within 30 days after you move out (unless you and the landlord agree otherwise).
• Landlord may keep up to one month’s rent for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | • Landlord must provide an itemized list of deductions.
• If you dispute, you can file a claim in small‑claims court. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain the premises in a safe, livable condition (e.g., plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity). | • If the landlord fails to fix major problems, you can withhold rent *only* if the issue is serious and the landlord has been notified in writing. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑payment of rent: 3‑day written notice before eviction.
• For lease termination: 30‑day notice for month‑to‑month tenants; 60‑day for longer leases. | • Notice must be in writing and delivered personally or via certified mail. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must file a lawsuit in district court.
• You’ll receive a summons and have 5 days to respond.
• Court will set a hearing; if you win, the landlord must pay damages. | • Eviction cannot be used for retaliation or discrimination. | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Protected classes: race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, age, source of income, etc. | • Texas law prohibits landlords from refusing to rent or charging higher rates based on these factors. | | **Right to Privacy** | • Landlord must give at least 24 hours’ notice before entering your unit, except in emergencies. | • Exceptions: repairs, inspections, showing the unit to prospective tenants/buyers. | | **Lease Terms** | • Written lease is required for month‑to‑month agreements.
• Landlord cannot unilaterally change lease terms without your consent. | • Any changes must be documented in writing and signed by both parties. | | **Rent Increases** | • No statutory limit on how much a landlord can raise rent, but they must give proper notice (usually 30 days for month‑to‑month). | • For fixed‑term leases, rent can only increase at the end of the lease term unless otherwise agreed. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major problem after notice, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from rent (only for serious issues). | • Keep receipts and document the problem. | | **Legal Remedies** | • Small‑claims court for disputes under $10,000.
• Texas Attorney General’s Office for consumer protection complaints.
• Local housing agencies for code enforcement. | • You can also seek mediation or arbitration if your lease provides for it. | #### Quick Checklist Before Moving In 1. **Get a written lease** – even if you’re renting month‑to‑month. 2. **Ask for a copy of the security deposit receipt** – it should include the amount and the deadline for return. 3. **Document the condition of the unit** – take photos or videos before you move in. 4. **Know the local ordinances** – some cities (e.g., Austin, Dallas) have additional tenant protections beyond state law. #### Resources - **Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA)** – tenant‑landlord handbook. - **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division** – complaint filing. - **Local tenant unions or advocacy groups** – e.g., “Texas Tenants Union.” - **Small‑claims court website** – for filing disputes. --- **Bottom line:** As a Texas tenant, you’re protected against unfair eviction, discrimination, and unsafe living conditions. Keep all communications in writing, know the notice periods, and don’t hesitate to use the legal remedies available if your landlord violates your rights.
